title: Variant granularization, fallback ranking, and published profile matrix for GPU families
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Create a reproducible process and published artifact set for hardware-specific performance profiles across A100/H100/L40S/MI300 that supports: (1) fine-grained variant granularization (memory/clock/driver bins), (2) explicit fallback ranking for runtime routing and graceful degradation, (3) signed profile publication and automated canary calibration. Goals: enable model onboarding to surface deterministic latency/cost expectations per GPU family, reduce live re-pinning incidents, and provide a machine-readable profile matrix consumed by the serving runtime and Console.
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative profile JSON produced for each model+variant on A100/H100/L40S/MI300 with fields: sku, driver_hash, seq_length_buckets, p50/p95 generation latency (ms), tokens_per_sec, batch_efficiency, warm_cold_delta, memory_headroom_percent, quantization_compatibility_tags
Runtime can ingest profile JSON and compute fallback ordering for a given request within 50ms of decision time in unit tests
Canary calibration job that compares live p95 vs published p95 and marks profiles as STABLE/DEGRADED with thresholds (p95 increase > 15% or jitter > 20%)
Publish workflow writes signed profile manifest to artifacts store and updates public profile index used by Console
Automated unit and integration tests for cold-warm behavior, kernel selection replay, and prefix-cache effect included in CI
Documentation page for profile taxonomy and pin reversion playbook published in Confluence and linked from onboarding flow
test_plan: 1) Offline benchmark suite: run 10,000 sample traces across seq=[64,128,512] and batch sizes [1,4,8] on each GPU SKU to produce profile metrics. 2) Canary: deploy profile to 5% of traffic on dedicated pool, collect 48h p50/p95 and compare to published signature. 3) Regression: run quantization sensitivity matrix for int8/4-bit paths and ensure quality delta < 3% for eval prompts. 4) Ingestion tests: inject malformed profile and verify runtime rejects with clear error and falls back to family-level profile.
engineering_notes: Proposal: add new 'fallback_score' computed from weighted sum of (p95_latency, cost_per_token, stability_score). Weights default to (0.6, 0.2, 0.2) but configurable per customer tier.
Decision: use driver_hash + cuda_version + kernel_patch_level as the stability fingerprint rather than exact driver string to reduce churn from unrelated driver metadata.

Trade-offs: very fine-grained bins reduce incorrect pinning but increase profile churn and storage. We'll cap granularity to 4 bins per SKU (e.g., high-clock, baseline, thermally-throttled, microcode-rev).

Performance thresholds: baseline p95 targets: A100 p95 < 38ms (seq64), H100 p95 < 30ms, L40S p95 < 35ms, MI300 p95 < 40ms for batch=1. These are starting points and will be tuned after first public run.

Failure mode: when signature verification fails, runtime should prefer: 1) same family pinned variant, 2) fallback to family-generic profile, 3) route to lower-tier model if cost SLO breached. This policy will be enforced in the routing policy engine with a 3-level priority queue.
Implementation outline: bench-runner -> profile-synthesizer -> signer -> profile-indexer. Profile JSON schema v1 attached in Confluence draft.
Required infra: ephemeral bench nodes for each SKU, secure signing key in KMS (rotate quarterly), artifact bucket with immutability flag for signed manifests.
risks: Profile churn causing frequent re-pinning and potential regressions during large model rollouts
Mis-calibrated p95 thresholds leading to over-eager fallbacks and degraded quality
Insufficient bench coverage for rare seq lengths causing surprises in tail latency

notes_for_release_notes: Introduced hardware-specific published performance profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300). Profiles enable deterministic routing, explicit fallback ranking, and signed manifests for auditability. Initial profiles are experimental and will be gated behind runtime feature flag 'hw_profile_v1'.
